capital.name: Beirut
capital.shortDescription: A layered coastal capital known for food, music, publishing, nightlife, and a distinctive Mediterranean-Arab energy.

prompts.prompt: Warm flatbread dusted with za'atar. A band that made Arab indie feel sharper, riskier, and more alive. A small Mediterranean country with a cedar on its flag. Which country is it?
This country is often associated with tabbouleh, kibbeh, and long mezze tables. Which is it?
Fairuz is one of the most beloved voices connected to which country?

reveal.intro: Lebanon feels intimate and expansive at once: mountain and sea, morning music and late-night city energy, generous food and sharp artistic presence. Its cultural footprint is much larger than its size suggests.

heroImage.alt: Beirut waterfront with the city and Mediterranean in view

funFacts: The cedar tree has symbolized Lebanon for centuries and still anchors the country's visual identity.
In many Arab homes, Fairuz is part of the sound of morning, not just a historical singer on a playlist.
Beirut has long carried a reputation for publishing, nightlife, and cultural intensity well beyond its size.

items.name: Man'oushe
items.description: Warm flatbread baked with za'atar or cheese and eaten in the kind of everyday way that tells you more about a place than a banquet ever could.
items.whyItMatters: This is the kind of breakfast that makes Lebanon feel immediate and lived-in: quick, fragrant, comforting, and communal.

items.name: Mashrou' Leila
items.description: Sharp, literate, restless, and emotionally exposed, Mashrou' Leila opened up a contemporary sound that felt urban, intimate, confrontational, and unmistakably alive.

items.name: An Unnecessary Woman
items.creator: Rabih Alameddine
items.description: A brilliant, solitary woman in Beirut, a lifetime of reading, and a city felt through intellect, memory, and mood.

items.name: Jeita Grotto
items.description: A limestone cave system of cathedral-like chambers and underground water that feels almost unreal the first time you see it.
items.whyItMatters: It widens the picture of Lebanon beyond city life and ruins, into something geologic, luminous, and almost mythic.

items.name: Saloua Raouda Choucair
items.description: A pioneering modern artist whose abstract forms made Arab modernism feel architectural, rhythmic, and unmistakably her own.

items.name: Beirut
items.description: Beirut is a city of sea views, layered history, book culture, nightlife, and restaurants that make food feel like a social art.
